text.p: India's state-run State Trading Corp (STC) on Tuesday denied a newspaper report that imported wheat from Australia was contaminated.
The Financial Express said on Monday that the Agriculture Ministry had warned that recent imports of Australian wheat "may be contaminated and the situation may well be alarming".
The daily newspaper said the ministry's plant quarantine division had said there was evidence of "exotic weed seeds" in wheat samples taken at Indian ports.

It said authorities had decided to divert the wheat to southern India, where the grain is not grown, and to prevent it from reaching the northern or western sections to avoid infecting India's own crop.
STC said in a statement that the newspaper "gives an erroneous impression that the imported wheat is infected".

"This is far from the truth. The Australian wheat has one of the highest quality standards and has been permitted for distribution in India only after proper inspection and trading," the statement said.
STC said the entire quantity of 1.4 million tonnes of Australian wheat, which had already arrived in India, had been fully tested by the Australian Wheat Board before shipment.
After arriving at Indian ports, the wheat was again tested by the Indian government and released for public distribution after being cleared by the state-run Food Corporation of India (FCI), it said.

STC said the presence of "weed" in wheat from any source was not unusual, and Indian plant protection and quarantine authorities had taken precautionary measures, including pre-shipment inspection by Indian authorities at loading ports.
It did not indicate whether the shipments had been diverted to southern India.

In December, India authorised STC to import two million tonnes of wheat to build stocks and check rising prices. STC officials said they had so far contracted to import 1.75 million tonnes, mainly from Australia, Argentina and Canada.
STC said the entire quantity had already arrived at the Indian ports.
Agriculture Ministry officials were unavailable for comment.
